record.original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+1}-free, where W_{2k+1} is the odd wheel on 2k+1 vertices, must the extremal graph for lambda(G) depend only on the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, taking the complete join K_k \/ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the other residue classes?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.44. Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large, and G is a W2k+1-free graph with m edges.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a fixed integer. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix (the spectral radius). The odd wheel $W_{2k+1}$ is the graph on $2k+1$ vertices obtained by joining a single vertex to every vertex of a cycle of length $2k$. For two graphs $A$ and $B$, let $A \vee B$ denote their join (the disjoint union together with all edges between $V(A)$ and $V(B)$), and let $tK_1$ denote the empty graph on $t$ vertices. For integers $a \ge 1$, $\ell \ge 1$, and $k \ge 2$, define $S^{1,\ell}_{a,k}$ to be the graph obtained from $K_k \vee aK_1$ by selecting one vertex $v$ of the $K_k$-part and attaching $\ell$ pendant vertices to $v$ (so $v$ has $\ell$ extra neighbors of degree $1$).

Consider the class of $W_{2k+1}$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges, and let an extremal graph be one that maximizes $\lambda(G)$ over this class.

Prove or disprove the following: there exists $m_0 = m_0(k)$ such that for every $m \ge m_0$, every extremal graph is determined (up to isomorphism) only by the residue class of $m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2}$ modulo $k$, and is given by
\[
G^*_m \;=\; \begin{cases} K_k \vee \left(\tfrac{m}{k} - \tfrac{k-1}{2}\right) K_1 & \text{if } k \mid m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2}, \\[4pt] S^{1,\ell}_{\tfrac{m-\ell}{k} + \tfrac{k+3}{2},\, k} & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases}
\]
where in the non-divisible case $\ell \in \{1,2,\dots,k-1\}$ is chosen so that $m - \ell$ makes the indicated formula a non-negative integer corresponding to the residue class of $m + \tfrac{k(k+1)}{2} \pmod k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns the edge-version (graphs with a fixed number of edges $m$) of the spectral Turán problem for odd wheels. While the vertex-version (graphs with $n$ vertices) has been largely resolved for $k \ge 2$, $k \notin \{4,5\}$, and recent work has addressed $k \in \{4,5\}$, the edge-version stated here is reported as still open in the source listing the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The spectral radius of graphs with no odd wheels
status_evidence.snippet: Determines spectral extremal graphs in SPEX(n, W_{2k+1}) for k>=3, k not in {4,5}, sufficiently large n.
status_evidence.claim: The vertex (n-vertex) spectral extremal problem for odd wheels is largely solved, but this is distinct from the edge (m-edge) version stated in the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: More results on the spectral radius of graphs with no odd wheels
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses the remaining cases k in {4,5} for the n-vertex spectral extremal problem for W_{2k+1}.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues on the n-vertex problem; no source resolving the edge-extremal conjecture was found.
